hero.lead: A nation of 101.6 million whose stock market joined the FTSE emerging-market indices in September 2026, and where nine in ten cook with clean fuel.

stats.label: Portfolio flows from the index upgrade, World Bank estimate

capital.heading: 24 instruments. Flood defences, roads, ports and wastewater, power for the south, and credit for small businesses.

record.text: Public and publicly guaranteed debt at the end of 2024, as a share of GDP: IMF staff estimate in the 2025 Article IV consultation
Just Energy Transition Partnership, declared 14 December 2022: at least $15.5 billion to be mobilised over three to five years, half public and half private
Three IBRD loans approved in September 2026: Hai Phong City Resilience, Mekong Resilient Regional Connectivity and Sustainable Fisheries Development
JICA programme loan for green transformation, green growth and climate resilience, signed 30 March 2026: 1.5% a year over 15 years
Portfolio flows the upgrade to FTSE emerging-market status could bring in the first few years, a World Bank estimate; 27 stocks joined the FTSE Global All Cap index on 21 September 2026

register.name: Sustainable Fisheries Development Project
register.detail: Approved 14 September 2026 · IBRD loan · Nine fishing ports across the North, Central and Mekong Delta regions
register.note: More than 525,000 fishers, aquaculture farmers and coastal residents; women at least half of direct beneficiaries
register.text: An IBRD loan to modernise nine fishing ports and build infrastructure and capacity for sustainable, climate-resilient fishing and aquaculture. It serves the food and livelihood standards of Vietnam’s coastal communities.

register.name: Mekong Resilient Regional Connectivity Project
register.detail: Approved 9 September 2026 · IBRD loan · 251 km of key Mekong Delta highways rehabilitated to international road safety standards
register.note: Year-round connectivity for about 856,800 direct users
register.text: An IBRD loan to rehabilitate 251 kilometres of key highways in the Mekong Delta, so that farmers can move their goods even in heavy rain. Construction is expected to create about 10,900 jobs a year; the roads serve the livelihood and food standards.

register.name: Hai Phong City Resilience Development Project
register.detail: Approved 4 September 2026 · IBRD loan · A new section of Ring Road 3, wastewater treatment and flood protection
register.note: More than 311,000 residents to benefit
register.text: An IBRD loan for a new section of Ring Road 3 to shorten truck journeys, more wastewater treatment, and flood protection for the historic centre of Hai Phong. Wastewater treatment serves the shelter standard, measured by safely managed sanitation, which sets Vietnam’s Coverage.

register.name: REDD-plus results-based payments for the results period of 2014 (FP294)
register.detail: Approved by the GCF Board at its 44th meeting, 25 to 28 March 2026 · Decision B.44/11 · Accredited entity: JICA
register.note: USD 71,955,000 for verified forest emission reductions
register.text: Green Climate Fund payments to Vietnam for results already achieved in reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation, with the results verified by the UNFCCC. The proceeds are to be reinvested to tackle the drivers of deforestation and forest degradation, which serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Integrated Resilient Development Project
register.detail: Approved 30 September 2025 · IBRD loans of $144.97 million · Total cost $228.54 million, with $83.57 million from the provinces
register.note: Flood protection in Da Nang and year-round roads in Gia Lai
register.text: IBRD loans for civil works: river dredging and riverbank protection, a flood bypass channel and new bridges in Da Nang, and raised roads and bridges in Gia Lai that link the Central Highlands to Quy Nhon Port and serve as evacuation routes. It protects the shelter and livelihood standards.

register.name: Emission reduction in the Central Highlands and South Central Coast (RECAF, FP250)
register.detail: Approved 24 October 2024 · GCF grant · Accredited entity: IFAD · Funded activity agreement effective 26 February 2026 · Estimated completion 26 February 2032
register.note: Total value $96.1 million with co-financing
register.text: A Green Climate Fund grant, through IFAD, for forest conservation and deforestation-free value chains such as coffee, pepper, bamboo and fruit. It is to improve 145,000 hectares through agroforestry and community forest management, which serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Binh Duong Province Water Environment Improvement Project
register.detail: Approved 12 January 2024 · Total investment $311 million, with $80 million from the Government budget · Thuan An, Di An and Tan Uyen
register.note: About 550,000 residents by 2032
register.text: World Bank financing to expand sewage collection and treatment in three cities of Binh Duong; in Tan Uyen, wastewater services are to rise from under 10% to 32%. It serves the shelter standard, measured by safely managed sanitation, which sets Vietnam’s Coverage.

register.name: Climate Adaptation Through Irrigation Modernization Project
register.detail: Signed 3 September 2026 · ADB loan of $40.66 million from ordinary capital resources · Grants of $1.5 million (Japan Fund for Prosperous and Resilient Asia and the Pacific) and $600,000 (High-Level Technology Fund)
register.note: Seven irrigation systems in Dong Nai, Gia Lai and Quang Ngai
register.text: Modernises seven irrigation systems and improves water management, raising cultivable irrigated land with a reliable water supply to 21,941 hectares and land for high-value crops and crop diversification to 11,399 hectares. About 295,500 people benefit directly, which serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Climate Resilient Inclusive Infrastructure for Ethnic Minority Project II
register.detail: Signed 17 April 2025 · ADB loans of $59 million · $1 million grant from the High-Level Technology Fund · Phu Yen and Quang Tri
register.note: About 363,000 people, 187,000 of them from ethnic minority groups
register.text: Upgrades about 133 kilometres of district and commune roads to climate-resilient standards, builds and upgrades rural water supply systems, and funds climate and weather data for early warning. It serves the water and livelihood standards.

register.name: O Mon III Combined Cycle Power Plant Construction Project (I)
register.detail: Signed 9 November 2026, Tokyo · Japanese ODA loan · 1.4% a year (0.01% for consulting services), 30 years, 10 years’ grace · Executing agency: Vietnam National Industry - Energy Group
register.note: Up to JPY 27,901 million
register.text: A JICA loan for a gas-fired combined cycle power plant in O Mon District, Can Tho City, with consulting services, to improve power supply capacity in southern Vietnam. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Project for Disaster Resilient Rural Development
register.detail: Signed 1 May 2026, Hanoi · Japanese ODA loan · 2.25% a year, 30 years, 10 years’ grace · Lao Cai, Dien Bien, Tuyen Quang, Son La and Lai Chau
register.note: JPY 21,590 million
register.text: A JICA loan for small-scale infrastructure in five northern provinces, with 90 subprojects currently envisaged: 41 road, 29 irrigation and 20 riverbank protection works. It is to raise agricultural productivity, improve livelihoods and reduce damage from natural disasters, which serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Climate Adaptive Infrastructure for Ethnic Minority Communities in the North Mountain and Midland Area
register.detail: Signed 1 May 2026, Hanoi · Japanese ODA loan · 2.30% a year, 30 years, 10 years’ grace · Tuyen Quang, Thai Nguyen, Lang Son and Cao Bang
register.note: JPY 17,666 million
register.text: A JICA loan for small-scale infrastructure in four provinces of the northern mountainous region, with 28 subprojects currently envisaged: 19 road, 7 irrigation and 2 water supply works, to support production in ethnic minority communities. It serves the water, food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Program Loan for Green Transformation toward Green Growth and Climate Resilience
register.detail: Signed 30 March 2026, Hanoi · Japanese ODA programme loan · 1.5% a year, 15 years, 5 years’ grace · Built on a Policy Matrix agreed by the Government and JICA
register.note: Up to JPY 50,000 million
register.text: A JICA programme loan, with policy dialogue, for three areas of reform: fiscal and investment incentives for green growth, the policies that carry out Vietnam’s Nationally Determined Contribution, and adaptation to climate change. It supports the energy standard and protects the others from climate risk.

register.name: Tri An Hydropower Plant Expansion Project
register.detail: Signed 24 June 2025, Frankfurt · Direct loan to EVN without a Government guarantee, the first such KfW project for EVN · Design capacity 200 MW
register.note: Built alongside the existing Tri An hydropower plant
register.text: A KfW loan to Viet Nam Electricity (EVN) for a 200 MW expansion of the Tri An hydropower plant. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: 500 kV transmission lines and substations, Binh Duong and Dong Nai
register.detail: Credit Facility Agreement signed 26 May 2025 · AFD to EVN National Power Transmission Corporation (EVN NPT)
register.note: A step towards the public finance commitments of the Just Energy Transition Partnership, according to the UK and the EU
register.text: An Agence Française de Développement credit facility to EVN NPT to build 500 kV transmission lines and substations across Binh Duong and Dong Nai provinces. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Just Energy Transition Partnership
register.detail: Political declaration 14 December 2022 · At least $15.5 billion over 3 to 5 years · $7.75 billion public finance from the International Partners Group and at least $7.75 billion private finance through GFANZ
register.note: An initial amount to be mobilised; a political commitment, not a binding agreement
register.text: A partnership between Vietnam and the International Partners Group to move towards at least 47% of electricity generation from renewables by 2030, and towards a peak of 30.2 GW of coal power, down from 37 GW planned. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: HDBank loan for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises
register.detail: Signed 7 July 2026 · ADB mandated lead arranger and co-coordinator with Standard Chartered Bank (Singapore) · 29 commercial banks mobilised an additional $621 million
register.note: At least 40% of ADB’s financing for women-owned MSMEs
register.text: An ADB loan to Ho Chi Minh City Development Joint Stock Commercial Bank (HDBank) for medium- and long-term lending to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises under its sustainable finance framework. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: IFC senior loans to VPBank for small and medium enterprises
register.detail: Approved 27 March 2026 · Signed 20 May 2026 · Invested 29 June 2026 · 5-year senior loan of up to $100 million and 7-year senior loan of up to $50 million
register.note: Part of a funding package of up to $830 million
register.text: IFC lending to Vietnam Prosperity Joint Stock Commercial Bank (VPBank) to grow its lending to small and medium enterprises, with a focus on women-led and women-owned SMEs and SMEs in agriculture. It serves the livelihood and food standards.

register.name: BIDV sustainable agriculture and women-owned SME financing
register.detail: Signed 19 December 2025 · ADB $100 million, CANPA $20 million, JICA $50 million and three commercial banks $80 million · ADB mandated lead arranger and bookrunner
register.note: ADB’s own loan of $100 million from ordinary capital resources
register.text: A syndicated package arranged by ADB for BIDV to lend to agribusinesses for sustainable production, climate adaptation and resource efficiency, and to women-owned small and medium-sized enterprises. It serves the food and livelihood standards.
by: Canadian Climate and Nature Fund for the Private Sector in Asia

register.name: IFC subscription to a VPBank sustainability bond
register.detail: Approved 8 April 2025 · Signed 8 August 2025 · Invested 15 September 2025 · Five-year bond, up to $200 million
register.note: Proceeds for eligible climate and social projects
register.text: IFC subscribed to a five-year VPBank sustainability bond whose proceeds expand the bank’s sustainable finance portfolio, for eligible climate and social projects under its Sustainable Finance Framework. It serves the energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: Bau Bang water treatment plant expansion, Thu Dau Mot Water
register.detail: Loan agreement signed 4 August 2025 · JICA co-financing of an equivalent amount
register.note: Capacity raised from 30,000 to 80,000 cubic metres a day
register.text: An ADB loan to Thu Dau Mot Water Joint Stock Company to expand the Bau Bang water treatment plant, for a reliable supply of clean water to residents and to commercial and industrial users. It serves the water standard.

register.name: IFC senior loan to HD Saison Finance for green and productive micro loans
register.detail: Approved 2 April 2025 · Signed 18 June 2025 · Invested 21 July 2025 · 3-year senior loan of up to $50 million
register.note: At least half for electric two-wheelers and energy-efficient goods
register.text: IFC lending to HD Saison Finance for micro loans to low-income people across Vietnam: at least half for electric two-wheelers and energy-efficient consumer durables, the rest for two-wheelers used for work or business. It serves the livelihood and energy standards.

register.name: AIIB on-lending facility to VPBank for sustainable infrastructure
register.detail: Approved 22 August 2024 for $150 million · $100 million facility signed, announced 16 July 2025 · Commitment now $150 million, according to AIIB · Nonsovereign
register.note: The second AIIB facility with VPBank; a significant portion earmarked for climate finance
register.text: An Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank on-lending facility to VPBank to promote sustainable infrastructure and support climate mitigation in Vietnam. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Vinschool Sustainable Education Project
register.detail: Signed 18 March 2025 · Syndicated sustainability-linked loan · ADB $40 million, LEAP 2 $35 million, ILX $40 million, Emerging Africa & Asia Infrastructure Fund $35 million
register.note: Educational facilities for 20,400 students in urban areas of Ha Noi, Ho Chi Minh City and Hung Yen
register.text: The first sustainability-linked loan in Vietnam’s education sector, according to ADB, to expand the Vinschool system, which serves more than 48,000 students across 54 campuses. It serves the education standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 39 in every hundred live in towns and cities; the rest live on the land they farm and fish.
items.alt: A busy street in Hanoi with motorbikes

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in farms and pasture
items.text: The land that feeds the nation, and the first place a citizen dividend can be earned.
items.alt: Green rice terraces in the northern highlands of Vietnam

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest
items.text: Standing forest holds the water, soil and carbon that the world will pay to keep.
items.alt: Tropical forest in Cuc Phuong National Park, Vietnam

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person
items.text: Enough to supply every home, once it is stored, treated and piped.
items.alt: The Mekong Delta, Vietnam, wooden boats on a wide brown river

items.name: The Power
items.label: Of electricity from renewables, 2023
items.text: Water, sun and wind already make almost half of the nation’s electricity; the rest is the opportunity.
items.alt: A solar farm in Ninh Thuan province, Vietnam

items.name: TTC AgriS
items.text: Thanh Thanh Cong - Bien Hoa Joint Stock Company is a major local agricultural enterprise and a comprehensive agriculture solutions provider, according to IFC. In June 2023 IFC and Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation announced that they would help arrange a $40 million commodity-backed warehouse finance facility for it, under IFC’s Global Warehouse Finance Program.

items.name: Thu Dau Mot Water
items.text: Thu Dau Mot Water Joint Stock Company signed a $6 million ADB loan in August 2025, with JICA co-financing an equivalent amount, to expand the Bau Bang water treatment plant. The expansion raises the plant’s capacity from 30,000 to 80,000 cubic metres a day.

items.name: SeABank
items.text: Southeast Asia Commercial Joint Stock Bank received a $100 million IFC investment in February 2023 to widen access to housing loans for lower- and middle-income families. SeABank expected to at least double the number of its lower- and mid-end housing loans by 2026.

items.name: Viet Nam Electricity (EVN)
items.text: Signed a €65 million loan agreement with KfW in Frankfurt on 24 June 2025, a direct loan without a Government guarantee and the first such KfW project for EVN. It finances the Tri An Hydropower Plant Expansion, with a design capacity of 200 MW, built alongside the existing plant.

items.name: Vinschool
items.text: Serves more than 48,000 students across 54 campuses. In March 2025 it signed a $150 million syndicated sustainability-linked loan with ADB, the first in Vietnam’s education sector according to ADB, to provide educational facilities for 20,400 students in urban areas of Ha Noi, Ho Chi Minh City and Hung Yen.

items.name: FV Hospital
items.text: Began operations in District 7, Ho Chi Minh City, on 11 March 2003, and has cared for more than 6 million patients since. It offers more than 45 medical and surgical specialities and has been awarded JCI international accreditation four times in a row, from 2016 to 2025.

items.name: HDBank
items.text: Ho Chi Minh City Development Joint Stock Commercial Bank lends to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises under its sustainable finance framework. In July 2026 it signed a $100 million ADB loan, at least 40% of it for women-owned businesses, alongside $621 million from 29 commercial banks.
